clue.text: The last word down? You need to correct errors!

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

explanation.surface: Someone declares the matter closed and insists that mistakes must be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word down?' reads like a final ruling; it is AMEN, the word that ends a prayer, followed by D for down.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to revise it and remove its mistakes.

clue.text: Working around Conservative America in a particular case

indicators.note: around means the word for working is wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: active means working, in operation
USA is America

explanation.surface: A Tory and America are being worked around in some specific matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a legal matter or an instance; it is a grammatical case, the one for direct objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The accusative is one of the grammatical cases, used for the object of a verb.

clue.text: Attention paid in the army

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words the army

explanation.surface: Soldiers are made to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone your ear is to listen to them attentively.

clue.text: River bird, one living by rock?

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A river bird nests among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests a crag by the river; it is rock music, which a disc jockey plays for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey makes a living playing records, rock among them.

clue.text: Perhaps Siamese beer leads to time I lost in tipsy trance-like state

parts.note: a Siamese is an example of a cat
ale is a beer

indicators.note: lost in says some letters go missing from the word tipsy

explanation.surface: Drinking leaves someone tipsy and then in a stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost in' removes T (time) and I from TIPSY, leaving PSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalepsy is a medical condition of rigid, trance-like unresponsiveness.

clue.text: Copy malt's modified cell material

indicators.note: modified signals that the letters of copy malt's are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A distiller copies a malt whisky, altering its ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: Cytoplasm is the substance filling a living cell around the nucleus.

clue.text: Take most of strain, breaking bones

indicators.note: breaking signals the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged
most of means the word strain loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Under too much strain, bones break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the N of STRAIN to leave STRAI, which 'breaking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the bones of the ankle and upper foot.

clue.text: Street lamps perhaps spoiling and obscuring what's above

indicators.note: in a down answer what is above is the top letter, so the first letter is hidden away

parts.note: blighting means spoiling or ruining

explanation.surface: Streetlights ruin the view and hide the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscuring what's above' removes the top (first) letter B of BLIGHTING in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Street lamps are an example of public illumination.

clue.text: Beans perhaps preserved in various oils

definitions.text: Beans perhaps preserved in various oils

parts.words: Beans perhaps preserved in various oils
parts.note: bean is slang for a head, so heads captured in oil paint describes painting people's likenesses

explanation.surface: Tins of beans are kept in different cooking oils.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture misleads: bean is slang for head, and oils are oil paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of painting likenesses, often heads in oil paint.

clue.text: Small boat dragged up on old sailor's cry

indicators.note: in a down entry dragged up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal vessel

explanation.surface: A dinghy is hauled ashore to an old seaman's shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Yo-ho is the traditional shout of pirates and seamen hauling ropes.

clue.text: Come in after fish and chips

indicators.note: after says the word for come in follows the fish

parts.note: carp is a fish
enter means come in

explanation.surface: Fish and chips arrive at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish and chips' reads as the meal; Chips is a traditional nickname for a carpenter, who makes wood chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is the old nickname for a ship's woodworker, and by extension any joiner.

clue.text: A horse is saddled with one right around

definitions.text: A horse is saddled with one
definitions.meaning: the strap that holds a saddle on a horse
the measurement right around something, its circumference

explanation.definitionFit: Both the saddle strap under a horse and a measurement round the waist are this.

clue.text: One amateurishly covering canvas with newspaper and rope

parts.note: a Sunday is a newspaper published on Sundays
a painter is a rope for tying up a boat

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a tarpaulin with a newspaper and some rope.
explanation.walkthrough: A boat's painter is the rope at its bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist who paints in their spare time, without professional skill.

clue.text: When one's resolved deanery ways must change?

indicators.note: must change says the letters of deanery ways are rearranged

explanation.surface: A determined churchman insists that the habits of the deanery must change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like settled, but means making resolutions, which people do on 1 January.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of January is the day people traditionally make resolutions.

clue.text: Sporting event that's shut up most of Irish town

parts.note: pent means shut up or confined

indicators.note: most of means the town's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands

explanation.surface: A sports event has closed down much of an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-discipline athletics contest held at the Olympics.

clue.text: Thong, as we Scots introduced?

parts.note: the leather strap used in Scottish schools for punishment, a Scots word

explanation.surface: A Scot claims the thong was a Scottish invention.
explanation.walkthrough: The leather strap once used to punish Scottish schoolchildren, an item and word from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for the leather strap used as a school punishment.

clue.text: Chile, say, and how it doesn't look — to its borders?

parts.note: Chile is an example of a nation
Chile is famously long and narrow, so it does not look wide

explanation.surface: A geographer remarks on Chile's long thin shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanning a whole country, reaching every frontier.

clue.text: Working with the RAF?

definitions.meaning: serving in the RAF, one of the armed services

explanation.definitionFit: A machine still operating, or a person serving in the forces.

clue.text: Opposed to dead Oedipus's daughter

parts.note: anti means opposed to
gone means dead

explanation.surface: Someone opposed Oedipus's daughter after she died.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the child of Oedipus and heroine of Sophocles' tragedy.

clue.text: Struggle to take in alien words — eastern ones?

indicators.note: to take in means the word for struggle holds the other pieces

parts.note: vie means struggle or compete
ET, the film extra-terrestrial, is an alien
names are words

explanation.surface: A foreigner struggles to understand Oriental words.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'words': eastern ones are words of an Asian language.
explanation.definitionFit: The language spoken in an East Asian country, so words from the Far East.

clue.text: Only fair

definitions.meaning: merely, as in only a little
equitable, as in a fair decision

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both merely and equitable.

clue.text: The spirit of a city — conventional?

definitions.meaning: relating to the Conventions on the conduct of war

explanation.definitionFit: Old name for gin, a Swiss city, and the treaties on war named after it.

clue.text: Check appropriate to mortar for strengthening

parts.note: rein means check or restrain
for can mean suited or appropriate to
cement is a mortar

explanation.surface: A builder checks the right mix of mortar for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcement is making something stronger, or the support that does so.

clue.text: Went, angrily following breather

parts.note: a lung is what one breathes with

explanation.surface: Someone stormed off after a short rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest; it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling out of a room is to leave in anger.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on one hire-car

parts.note: to tax is to strain or make heavy demands on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is burdened by the cost of a rental car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a car hired with its driver.

clue.text: Monteverdi possibly giving out class sound

indicators.note: giving out means letters are given up and removed

parts.note: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer, so Claudio is a forename he had
CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A Monteverdi opera sounds out in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monteverdi possibly' points to his first name, CLAUDIO; removing CL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means relating to sound, as in recorded or broadcast sound.

clue.text: Heard you once stood for it being valid in all cases

definitions.text: Heard you once stood for it being valid in all cases

parts.words: Heard you once stood for it being valid in all cases
parts.note: the letter that sounds like you was the film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Someone recalls standing up for a principle that applies everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: British film certificate U, said like 'you', meant films for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying to every case without exception.

clue.text: Go on snow and slip endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: skid means slip or slide

explanation.surface: Someone goes out on the snow and keeps slipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding over snow on runners is the sport of skiing.

clue.text: University group for fast climbers?

definitions.meaning: a group of elite US universities
a league of ivy, a plant that climbs fast

explanation.definitionFit: A set of elite American colleges, and whimsically a league of the clinging plant.

clue.text: A right foreigner

parts.note: a lien is a legal right over another's property

explanation.surface: Someone calls a stranger a real foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from another country, legally a non-citizen.
